tone_statements.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2015. Lalo dialects across time and space: subgrouping, dialectometry, and intelligibility. (Asia-Pacific Linguistics 22.) Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics, ANU. (Eka sketch = §3.4, pp. 46–50.)
tone_statements.quote: Eka’s syllable template is (C)V(N)TP and NT, in which the optional initial is one of 22 consonants, an obligatory vowel (one of 11 vowels or 1 syllabic fricative), an optional nasal final /ŋ/, tone (one of 6), and phonation type (harsh or modal). [...] In addition to three contrastive pitch heights and two contrastive phonation types, Eka also has a low-rising contour tone. This tone is a result of Proto Lalo Tone *1 (a high level pitch) becoming a low-rising contour in almost all environments. [...] Eka’s high level tone is realised as high level word medially and as high falling in word final position. [...] Eka exhibits frequent tone sandhi, in contrast to CW-QY and MD.
tone_statements.locator: §3.4 Eka, p. 46 (syllable template) and p. 49 (tonal system, after Table 3-21 'Eka reflexes of Proto Lalo tones')
tone_statements.n_tones: 6 (low-rising 24, low 21, mid 33, low harsh 21, mid harsh 33, high 55~53)

tone_statements.citation: Yang, Cathryn (2012). Classifying Lalo languages: Subgrouping, phonetic distance, and intelligibility. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 35(2): 113-137.
tone_statements.quote: Eka, YL and MD descend directly from PLa and do not share in any Greater Lalo innovations. Instead, they show divergent developments that make them decidedly different from any other Lalo language. MD shows a set of rhyme innovations, Eka shows micro-splits in *1, *2, *H, and *L, and YL shows mergers of *1 and *3 to mid and *L and *H to high. [...] [Table 4, Group: Eka, Innovations:] a) *1 > low-rising/default b) splits in *1, *2, *H, *L to high level under various conditions

sources.note: Nothing about stress in Eka. §3.4 (pp. 74–79) gives Eka's syllable template (C)V(N)TP / NT with 6 tones x harsh/modal phonation, the tone reflexes of Proto-Lalo, and extensive tone sandhi (high tone 55 word-medial, 53 word-final; low 21 > 33 before low; 24 > 35 before low). Whole-text a full-text search for stress/accent/prominen/unstressed: the only 'stressed syllable' remark (p. 64) is about the Central Lalo variety CW-QY (Qingyun village), not Eka.

sources.note: Condensed journal version of the thesis classification: Proto-Lalo has three pitch heights in modal phonation (*1,*2,*3) and two harsh-phonation tones (*H,*L); Eka descends directly from Proto-Lalo and is defined by tonal innovations: *1 > low-rising by default, and splits of *1, *2, *H, *L to a high level tone under various (prefixal/initial) conditions ('micro-splits'), shared by no other Lalo language; tone is also weighted in the Levenshtein-distance comparison (per Yang & Castro 2008). No synchronic Eka tone table (that is in Yang 2010/2015).
